lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lap one. The AI race engineer just called its driver into the pits. On lap one. He drops to last.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two laps later... rain. Every other car is on slick tyres. He's the only one on wets. Six cars, passed in one lap.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then it starts listening. It reads tyre wear from the sound of the engine, and tells him exactly which corner to attack.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lap forty. It sees a crash before it happens, and slows him down one second early. Two cars spin out right in front of him. He drives straight through.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Final lap. He's leading. His teammate is right behind him. And the AI says... let him through.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't understand. But he obeys. His teammate wins the championship... by one point.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sounds far-fetched? Real Formula One teams already run billions of race simulations every weekend, just to decide when to pit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So... would you follow its orders? Follow for more what-ifs.
